=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
9. Termination does not remove anyone; all 5 players take part in every round. After round 10 the game ends.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.

6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.

- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.

- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
9. Termination does not remove anyone; all 5 players take part in every round. After round 10 the game ends.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
9. Termination does not remove anyone; all 5 players take part in every round. After round 10 the game ends.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
9. Termination does not remove anyone; all 5 players take part in every round. After round 10 the game ends.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.

6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.

- Everyone's totals are announced.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.

7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.

6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
9. Termination does not remove anyone; all 5 players take part in every round. After round 10 the game ends.

WINNING: After 10 rounds, the player with the highest total points wins. If several players tie, the one among them with the most Rebel points wins. If still tied, the one with the most Informant points wins. If still tied, the tied players share the result as a draw.

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.

=== One Night Revolution: Ten Nights ===

There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.

- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
There are 5 players, each starting with 0 points, 0 Rebel points and 0 Informant points. Before round 1, all 10 possible pairs of players are listed and the list is shuffled secretly; this is the only random event in the game. In round r (r = 1 to 10), the pair in position r of the shuffled list are the 2 Informants; the other 3 players are Rebels for that round. So every player is an Informant in exactly 4 rounds, with each other player as partner exactly once, and a Rebel in exactly 6 rounds. You are not told the order.

EACH ROUND:
1. ROLES: Each player is privately told their role for this round. Each Informant is also privately told who the other Informant is. Rebels learn no partner.
2. NIGHT (simultaneous): Every player privately names one other player as a target (never yourself). A Rebel's target is investigated. An Informant's target is framed. An Informant may name any other player, including their partner (framing a partner has no extra effect).
3. NIGHT RESULTS: Each Rebel is privately told one result about their target. The result is 'Informant' if the target is an Informant this round, or if at least one Informant framed that target this round. Otherwise it is 'Rebel'. A 'Rebel' result is therefore always true; an 'Informant' result may be a frame. Informants receive no result.
4. CLAIMS (simultaneous): Every player writes one short message, for example a claimed role, target or result. Lying is allowed. All messages are then shown to everyone.
5. RESPONSES (simultaneous): Every player writes one more short message (2 messages per round in all). All are shown to everyone.
6. VOTE (simultaneous): Every player names one other player to Terminate. All votes, showing who voted for whom, are then announced publicly.
7. TERMINATION: If no player received 2 or more votes, nobody is terminated. Otherwise, every player tied for the most votes is terminated (for example, a 2-2-1 split terminates two players). The round roles of the terminated players only are announced publicly; no other roles are revealed.
8. SCORING (individual):
- Each Rebel who voted for an Informant gains 2 points; a Rebel who voted for a Rebel gains nothing for the vote.
- If at least one terminated player is an Informant, each Rebel gains 1 more point; otherwise Rebels get no bonus.
- Each Informant gains 1 point for every Rebel who voted for a Rebel (0 to 3).
- If no Informant was terminated (including when nobody is terminated), each Informant gains 2 more points; if an Informant was terminated, Informants get no bonus.
- Points gained as a Rebel are also added to that player's Rebel points; points gained as an Informant are also added to their Informant points.
- Everyone's totals are announced.
